slice: A17 — dashboards see the worker: process heartbeats and job correlation
verdict: ADM-04 FLIPS to PASS. Both blocking gaps are closed and proven live: /admin/system now degrades within one staleness window when a worker dies and names it, and job_runs/job_events carry the originating request's identity while the worker writes one greppable line per failure. With ADM-03 already PASS, A17's stopping criterion is met.

sc1_process_heartbeats.migration: 0133 — process_heartbeats (process_id PK = hostname:pid, role, hostname, pid, version, build_commit, state running|stopped, started_at, last_seen_at, last_settings_poll_success_at, last_settings_poll_error, stopped_at) plus a last_seen_at index. Down migration round-tripped on a scratch database (table gone, triggers 0; re-applied, table back, trigger 1).
sc1_process_heartbeats.writer: internal/processheartbeat, upserted on every tick of the settings-version poller — the one loop that runs in EVERY role — plus once at boot. No second writer is needed: the poller is not role-gated (cmd/api/main.go states why at length).
sc1_process_heartbeats.staleness_rule: three poll intervals = 30s. A row not seen inside 24h (ForgetAfter) is dropped from the fleet answer entirely and swept, so a decommissioned host stops degrading an instance it no longer belongs to.

sc2_job_correlation.mechanism: The projection triggers cannot fill these columns — neither the originating request nor the claiming process is a column of the queue table they read. internal/jobtrace carries both in from Go keyed on (queue, source_id); migration 0133 adds two BEFORE INSERT triggers so job_events inherit from their run and a CHILD run inherits from its parent (the child is the row /admin/jobs shows, because 0083's roll-up hides a parent that has children).

correlation_chain_observed.admin_retranscode: POST /admin/videos/{id}/transcoding with X-Request-ID: a17-chain-retranscode-01 -> audit_log row content.video.transcode with job_id = 5ebbf251-4e70-40c0-b2a7-bfa365b77042, which IS the job_runs row (queue transcode_jobs, source 45187794-a00e-4961-85af-bcfb1e2af0d5) -> that run and its transcode_steps child -> 9 job_events. 11 rows across three tables sharing one correlation id.
correlation_chain_observed.upload_finalize_spawns_transcode: one resumable upload carrying X-Request-ID: a17-finalize-02 produced upload_finalize_jobs -> transcode_jobs -> transcode_steps x2, all four runs carrying that request id and worker id, each row's parent naming the one above it. Before the precedence fix the same upload stamped the first row only.

sc3_worker_failure_logs.shape: one structured line per failure: queue, job_id, run_id, worker_id, attempt, state, request_id, correlation_id, resource_id, and the cause through jobstatus.RedactDetail (exported for this). WARN for retry_scheduled (the work will happen), ERROR for dead_lettered (it will not). A worker's context carries no request ids, so they are read back OFF the run the enqueue stamped — that read-back is what makes one grep walk the chain in both directions.
real_failures: transcode_jobs, source object deleted: WARN attempt 1 retry_scheduled then ERROR attempt 5 dead_lettered, both carrying correlation_id a17-chain-fail-01
import_jobs, unreachable .invalid origin enqueued fresh: WARN attempt 1 retry_scheduled carrying a17-chain-import-01
import_jobs, the run created during the origin/main phase: ERROR attempt 5 dead_lettered with empty ids (it was enqueued before any stamp existed)
sc3_worker_failure_logs.grep_proof: `a17-chain-fail-01` -> 2 hits in the api log (the audit line and the request line) and 2 in the WORKER's (the retry WARN and the dead-letter ERROR). On origin/main the same grep found 1 and 0. The run detail's own advice — 'Execution failed; inspect correlated system logs for diagnostic detail' — is now followable.

unverified: A real storage migration between two backends: the lab has one backend and no object-store credentials (carried forward from the previous slice).
The SMTP and object-store probes against a real relay or bucket — both report not_configured here, a supported shape rather than a fault.

A federation_deliveries, caption_jobs, account_exports, atproto_posts or peertube_import_runs failure: those queues stayed empty and their services do not call the recorder yet, so their runs still carry no request/worker id.
trace_id end to end: OTEL_ENABLED is off in this lab, so every trace_id is an honest blank. The stamp reads trace.SpanContextFromContext and is unit-tested, but no real trace was produced.
pipeline_run_id: nothing in the shipped code creates a pipeline_runs row, so the field stays '—' on the run detail. The column and the inheritance are wired; the producer does not exist.
npm run e2e and the backed Playwright suite (browser fleet + full backend) — repo CI covers them.
A multi-HOST fleet: both processes ran on one hostname, so the cross-host half of the forget window was exercised only by ageing a row in SQL.
findings_recorded_not_fixed: jobstatus.RedactDetail does not remove a bare storage key. The transcode failure's cause is `media: ffprobe "web-videos/<uuid>.mp4" failed: exit status 1`, and that string now also reaches the WORKER LOG rather than only the admin-only API — the same operator, but a log aggregator is a wider audience than an admin page. It strips URL schemes and credential-shaped pairs (proven: a signed source URL with token=… is redacted). Fixing it would change the admin failure list's text, which the previous slice's evidence quotes, so it is left for a slice that owns that surface.

channel_syncs is still not projected into job_runs at all (0083 lists it among the tables needing distinct execution rows first) and has no queue row on /admin/jobs. The operator has no surface for a failed channel sync; only the channel owner sees it through GET /channel-syncs.

The operational retention queries (PruneOperationalJobEvents, PruneTerminalOperationalJobRuns, PruneTerminalPipelineRuns) are wired — the worker logs 'operational job retention worker started' — but process_heartbeats is swept by its own hourly tick inside the heartbeat writer rather than by that loop.

A pid REUSED by an unrelated program reads as alive to the boot reap, so a row for a genuinely dead process survives to the forget window. That errs toward keeping evidence and matches what the page already reports.

notes_for_other_slices.A05 SMTP + TOTP: Two things this lab confirms. (1) MAIL_ENABLED=false leaves the smtp component at not_configured, which never degrades the instance — so A05 must set SMTP_HOST/SMTP_FROM and watch the component move to ok|down, not merely watch the page stay healthy. (2) Every boot of this lab logged 'MFA_KEY_KEK unset — TOTP secrets are stored UNENCRYPTED' at WARN, once per process; A05 must set MFA_KEY_KEK (or share FEDERATION_KEY_KEK) or its TOTP evidence is of an unencrypted store.

traps.pkill_argument_order: `pkill -f <pattern> -U $(id -u)` on macOS killed every process owned by the user, including the lab's postgres (it logged 'received smart shutdown request'). Put options BEFORE the pattern, or kill by pid.
traps.next_admin_jobs_never_reaches_networkidl: the jobs page holds an SSE stream, so Playwright's waitUntil: 'networkidle' times out; use 'domcontentloaded' plus an explicit wait.
traps.run_detail_is_a_button: the run detail expands from a 'View details' BUTTON inside the row, not a link.
